title: How to play
lead: Three games to play with friends in the browser, nothing to install. Each one opens with a scene that explains the rule on the spot. Here it is all at once.

steps.x: The room votes on four themes, or the host types one. Every character must fit it.
Everyone picks a character for another player. The opening shows who picks for whom.
Everyone sees the cards on the table except their own. Yours faces away from you.
On your turn, ask about your card. The others answer yes, no or maybe.
Right guess, you found out. Whoever finds out first tops the podium.

whoAmI.tip: Tip: nicknames count as a right guess. “The Dark Knight” works for Batman.

steps.x: Everyone gets the same character. The impostor gets a similar one and doesn't even know. With 7 or more, there are two.
A question about your card: a scale, a colour, an emoji, a choice or one word. Nobody says the name.
Everyone sees what each person answered. Who stands out?
Point at suspects and confirm your vote. Most votes goes out. A tie sends nobody out.
A caught impostor tries to guess the group's card. The group wins when every impostor is out.

impostor.tip: Tip: don't know the card? “I don't know this one” swaps everyone's cards, up to twice, before any answer shows.

steps.x: Everyone starts with coins and bids, one lot at a time. A bid in the last 5 seconds puts 5 seconds back on the clock.

steps.t: Build a team without knowing what for
steps.x: Nobody knows the mission yet. You can trade characters after the auction.
Out comes the mission, like “get a cat down from the fridge”.
Arrange the pictures and write on the board. Everyone presents their team.
Each vote is a point, and the round's winner gets more. With 3 or more, someone can present and give the verdict.

whatFor.tip: Tip: heavy missions only come up in rooms that turn them on.

items.x: You can play without an account, as a guest.
Bring friends with the room's code or link, or join a public room.
The host sets clocks, tastes and themes before starting.
Every match gives XP. With an account, your level and badges stay on your profile.
